q: You deploy a bundle with `databricks bundle deploy -t dev`, and the dev target uses `mode: development`. The job has a daily schedule. What happens the next morning?
o: The job runs on schedule under its normal name
Nothing: in development mode the schedule is paused, and the job name has a `[dev your_name]` prefix
The deploy fails because schedules are not allowed in dev
The job runs as the production service principal
e: Development mode prefixes resource names and pauses schedules and triggers, so each developer gets an isolated copy that does not run on its own.

q: The same bundle must write to `dev_retail` in dev and `prod_retail` in prod. What is the intended way to do this?
o: Two copies of the job YAML, one per environment
An `if` statement in the notebook that checks the workspace URL
A variable `catalog` with a default, overridden in `targets.prod.variables`, used as `${var.catalog}`
A job parameter that the operator types in on every run
e: Variables are resolved at deploy time per target. The definitions stay identical; only the target's variable values differ.

q: Someone edits the schedule of a bundle-deployed job directly in the Jobs UI. What happens at the next `databricks bundle deploy` to that target?
o: The UI change is overwritten with the schedule from the YAML
The deploy fails with a conflict
The UI change is copied back into the YAML
The job is duplicated
e: Deploys are declarative: the workspace is made to match the bundle files. Change the YAML in Git instead.

q: Which identity should a CI/CD system use to deploy a bundle to production?
o: The personal access token of the team lead
A shared user account whose password is stored in the repository
Any workspace admin's account
A service principal authenticated with OAuth
e: A service principal is not tied to a person and can be given exactly the rights it needs. OAuth (a client secret or workload identity federation) avoids long-lived personal tokens.

q: Which check belongs in the pull request stage, before anything is deployed to a shared environment?
o: Integration tests that run the production job on production tables
Unit tests on pure functions with small inputs, plus `databricks bundle validate`
`databricks bundle destroy -t prod`
A full refresh of every pipeline
e: Unit tests and validation are fast and touch no shared data. Integration tests run after the merge on a staging target with real tables.
